messages:
maya: anyone seeing a big gang reshuffle in us-west1 during the window? tiny gpu pods went pending and we spilled to on-demand racks — cost jumped. :money_with_wings:
jonathan: saw the alerts. is this the warm-pool not filling or scheduler refusing placement because of taints/affinity?
maya: warm pool existed but was pinned to us-west1b/c of zone policy. us-west1a got a network maintenance and nodes were tainted 'egress-degraded=true:NoSchedule' so scheduler forced evictions. pasted kubectl short output:
```
NAME           READY STATUS   NODE            REASON
job-x-small-1  0/1   Pending  <none>          PodAffinity/requiredDuringScheduling
job-x-small-2  0/1   Pending  <none>          Toleration missing for taint egress-degraded
...
```
alin: hmm — that taint is new from the egress team during the flap; we purposely added NoSchedule to avoid broken network racks. but together with strict podAffinity (we force spread by rack) it leaves no combinatorial placements.
kevin: are these tiny GPU pods requiring gang scheduling? fractional gang?
maya: they request 1 gpu each but are launched in gangs (k-scheduler group) with required affinity to avoid cross-rack NVLINK mismatch. scheduler can't satisfy both "rack-spread" and avoid tainted nodes -> pending.
jonathan: can we fallback to a best-effort placement for low-priority tiny jobs? maybe use tolerations-with-limited-ttl or relax requiredDuringScheduling to preferredDuringScheduling for these jobs.
alin: quick mitigation: add a toleration for egress-degraded with operator:Exists on the warmpool nodes + mark the cheap tiny job queue as preemptible so they can use degraded racks temporarily. not ideal but reduces on-demand spill.
kevin: i'm worried about correctness for some workloads — we should target only the 'best-effort-gpu-small' queue.
sre-bot: ALERT summary: 3921456789 - us-west1a egress maintenance -> 118 pods Pending, 34 evicted, cost delta +120% for GPU on-demand across the day.
maya: action items: 1) alin to coordinate with egress team on temporary relax of NoSchedule in affected racks (or add explicit toleration whitelist) 2) jonathan/kevin to add a cluster-level policy that downgrades 'required' affinity to 'preferred' for best-effort-gpu-small 3) maya will open cost ticket and tag infra-costs.
jonathan: i'll prototype a mutation admission webhook that converts "required"->"preferred" for a label selector (best-effort-gpu-small) and test in staging.
alin: i'll ask egress to flip taint to NoExecute with short TTL once network is healthy; that'll let jobs finish or be requeued instead of staying Pending forever.
maya: thanks. also let's add a quick dashboard for "pending-gang-count" by zone so we catch this earlier.
kevin: +1, and drop a runbook entry for this case (taint + strict affinity -> spill to on-demand).
maya: opening thread ticket now and pinging finance for cost reclaim. :thumbsup:
